comments: MODEL COMPLEXITY ABLATION (platform_model_server.md step 3), 'medium' variant, bottleneck_ch=96 (default/Small is 64, see kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_stemstride1_eltwiselinear.json). Channel-width multiplier chosen as the scaling rule (vs. block-repeat count) since bottleneck_ch is already a first-class constructor param with zero other code changes needed. Everything else identical to the Small/current-best config: stem_stride=1, encoder_depth=1, bottleneck_kernel_size=3, dropout_rate=0.1, eltwise_act=linear. Scoped at 8x64 by default -- re-point config.ini at whichever resolution step 2 selects before launching the full Tiny/Small/Medium sweep, since this config has no dataset-path field of its own (train.py reads config.ini, not this file, for the data root). CAUTION: CLAUDE.md's prior width sweep (bc in {32,96,128,192}, checkpoints/8x64_width_sweep/) was run on the OLD pre-stem_stride=1 architecture and found a confound -- only bc=64 got full pretrained-weight transfer from the native checkpoint, so that sweep mostly measured transfer-loss, not capacity. This is a fresh sweep on the current (stem_stride=1/maxpool-downsample/eltwise-linear) architecture; if finetuning from the bc=64 8x64 checkpoint, expect the same confound to reappear for bc!=64 -- consider training from scratch for a cleaner capacity-only comparison, or use kurals/expand_bottleneck_width.py for partial-transfer init and flag the confound explicitly when reporting results either way. NOT YET TRAINED -- staged only, holding for go-ahead before spending GPU time.
